description: Team HASH is tackling the Flame in Freefall challenge at NASA Space Apps 2026 (Khulna). We are building an AI-powered solution to analyze microgravity combustion data and advance space fire safety. Our focus includes Machine Learning, Web Development, and Data Visualization. Open to passionate contributors ready to turn NASA open science data into impactful tools!
summary: ShunnoShikha AI (Team HASH) is a fire-safety mission control for spacecraft and exploration habitats, for NASA Space Apps' Flame in Freefall challenge. In microgravity, flames behave unlike Earth fires: no buoyancy, spherical diffusion flames, and flammability follows a U-shaped boundary. It turns NASA's Physical Science Informatics archive into safety intelligence: 401 harmonized flight tests from 13 studies (BASS/BASS-II, FLEX/FLEX-2, CFI, Saffire, SAME/DAFT, ACME BRE/CFI-G/E-FIELD, SPICE, SLICE) with hardware-facility tags, anomaly filtering, and physics-weighted ranking against Lunar, Mars, Gateway and spacesuit atmospheres. A 3-regime combustion digital twin (sustained burn, radiative extinction, blowoff) powers interactive 3D visuals: a station fire twin, flammability boundary manifold, single-sample flame chamber (up to 100% O2), and a PSI investigation galaxy with intra-study variable comparison. Partial-gravity modes (0.16g/0.38g) are bounded between 0g and 1g, citing ACME E-FIELD as proxy and previewing LUCI/FM2. An autonomous pre-ignition guard makes fire unable to start: ignition-kernel quench, crew-safe O2 conditioning, circuit isolation, and FLEX-based CO2/He dilution; a deterministic emergency module simulates spread, gated suppression and crew environmental risk. AI briefings cite live NASA sources; Earth spin-offs link findings to water-mist extinguishers, dust-immune detectors and firefighter gear. Educational simulation only - no hardware commanded.
details:
ShunnoShikha AI ("zero flame") is a web-based fire-safety mission control for spacecraft and exploration habitats. It harmonizes 401 microgravity combustion flight tests from 13 NASA PSI investigations (BASS/BASS-II, FLEX/FLEX-2, CFI, Saffire I–VI, SAME/SAME-R, DAFT/DAFT-2, ACME BRE/CFI-G/E-FIELD, SPICE, SLICE, FGM tomography) into one repository with hardware-facility tags (CIR, CIR+MDCA, MSG flow duct, Cygnus), sensor-anomaly filtering, and physics-weighted ranking against target atmospheres (ISS, Gateway, Lunar EVA, Mars, spacesuit). A three-regime combustion digital twin — sustained burn, radiative extinction, convective blowoff — computes the U-shaped flammability boundary from Damköhler and radiative-loss physics, with bounded partial-gravity modes (0.16 g Lunar, 0.38 g Mars). Four interactive Three.js scenes visualize it: a compartment-level station fire twin, the boundary manifold, a flame chamber (O2 to 100%, CFI-G 85% and spacesuit presets), and a 3D investigation galaxy where clicking two runs of one study diffs constant vs manipulated variables, geometry and sensors. On top sits an autonomous pre-ignition guard, armed by default: it vetoes ignition attempts, trims O2 enrichment into the crew-safe band, de-energizes ignition sources, and adds FLEX-derived CO2/He dilution — fire cannot start. If an operator explicitly stands it down, a deterministic emergency engine simulates ignition, spread, gated suppression, crew environmental risk and downloadable incident reports. A local multimodal AI agent answers with live citations from NASA PSI/NTRS pages, labeling observed data vs model extrapolation.

What benefits does it have? Prevention instead of reaction: ignition is quenched before flame exists while monitoring, logs and the clock stay live. Evidence-first decisions: every ranking and hypothesis traces to real flight tests with provenance URLs, and untested conditions carry uncertainty flags instead of guesses. Crew-safe by construction: O2 never below 19.5%, water only when approved + de-energized + oxygen-isolated, every emergency action and stand-down explicitly confirmed. Explainable and reproducible: SHAP attributions, fixed-step deterministic simulation, cited AI briefings. One interface for science, operations and teaching.

What is the intended impact? Safer Artemis, Gateway, Lunar and Mars habitats by converting archived flight evidence into pre-ignition safety policy; virtual experiment protocols that preview LUCI and FM2 partial-gravity campaigns; terrestrial spin-offs (fine-water-mist extinguishers, dual-wavelength dust-immune smoke detectors, better firefighter textiles); and a STEM tool for microgravity combustion.

Tools, languages, hardware, software used? Backend: Python 3, FastAPI/uvicorn, NumPy, pandas, XGBoost + TreeSHAP, OpenCV, PyTorch/Transformers/PEFT (LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B regime predictor), WebSocket telemetry. Frontend: TypeScript, React/Next.js 14, Three.js, Tailwind CSS. AI: local Ollama omni-model with ReAct tool calling plus live NASA PSI/NTRS retrieval. Hardware-in-the-loop: virtual Arduino Uno/ESP32 cabin sensors at 1 Hz (Wokwi-ready firmware) and an optional serial gateway for real sensors — live actuation locked. Developed on Apple Silicon with MPS acceleration; versioned with git.

How is your project creative? The core inversion: most fire systems detect and suppress; ShunnoShikha prevents ignition itself and proves it live (veto banner, green shockwave, ticking clock). The galaxy turns a data table into a comparable 3D evidence space; the bounded partial-gravity surrogate links ISS-era E-FIELD flame physics to future Lunar/Mars tests; an explicit "rocket propulsion out of scope" guardrail shows scientific discipline; and an Earth spin-off panel closes the loop from orbit to everyday life.

What factors did your team consider? Safety and honesty: everything is labeled educational simulation, no hardware is commanded, live mode locks actuation, and environmental time-to-critical is never presented as human survival. Data integrity: provenance classes (compiled flight tables, live fetches, curated summaries), anomaly filtering, source URLs. Human factors: crew O2 floor, PBA warnings for CO2/He dilution, confirmation dialogs, keyboard-accessible 3D, calm/white themes. Engineering: deterministic reproducibility, instanced rendering and debounced API calls for smooth 3D, and scope discipline — buoyancy-free PSI science, not gravity-independent rocket combustion.
